findings.problem: The prompt calls these 'routed' destinations, but the parser in src/briefing/lib/destinations.ts:47-52 only recognises Discovery Studio, Outbound Studio, Deal Workspace and Asset Builder, and only the actions new/refresh/alert. Three of the six examples the model is told to imitate (Cold Call Studio, Signal Console, Getting to Signed) return null from parseDestination, so MoveRow renders them as plain text with no link; the 'review'/'update' actions are dropped. Meanwhile 'Asset Builder' (not a shipped area) still parses. The quality gate's moves_routed check only tests that destination is non-empty, so nothing enforces the instruction. The operator sees a recommended action that names an area but cannot be opened, contrary to the prompt's own claim that these are routed.

findings.state: Synthesis draft/critique/revise/gate-repair prompts (BANNED_LINE) and runQualityGate; same in supabase/functions/briefing-pipeline/llm/synthesis-shared.ts:12 and :365
findings.current: BANNED_VOCABULARY is only corporate filler (leverage, unlock, revolutionize … streamline). The prompt adds: "Also avoid … private Antaeus ontology, and slogan-like copy."
findings.problem: The prompt tells the model to avoid 'private Antaeus ontology' without saying what it is, and the deterministic gate checks none of it. A model cannot know Antaeus's private vocabulary; worse, several of the migration-map terms are ordinary GTM jargon the model produces unprompted ('enterprise sales motion', 'hot account', 'pressure', 'the read', 'the move'). The spec requires searching prompts for and replacing instructions around heat, motion, pressure, one move, system saw/read, thread, decay, die etc. Nothing in the generation path prevents a Pattern such as 'Linear's B2B motion is coming — the read is pressure on your pipeline.' from passing the gate and rendering.
findings.governing: ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/11_AI_PROMPT_AND_GENERATOR_REWRITE_SPEC.md (search list; rules 9, 11); original-working-set/02_LANGUAGE_MIGRATION_MAP.md rows motion, heat, hottest, pressure, one move, system saw, read (noun), thread, decaying, dying
findings.proposed: In both prompt copies replace 'private Antaeus ontology' with an explicit list and replacements: "Do not use these as labels or explanations: 'motion' for the sales process (say sales process, pipeline or outreach); 'heat', 'hot', 'cold' for priority (say priority or recent activity); 'pressure' (say risk, urgency or priority); 'the read' or 'the move' as nouns (say assessment or recommended action); 'dying', 'decay' (say the observable change, e.g. no activity for 21 days)." Add a separate deterministic check (both copies) for the phrase-level items that are unambiguous in generated analysis — 'the read', 'the move', 'one move', 'system saw', 'dying', 'heat score' — so they fail the gate and trigger repair; leave ordinary words such as 'motion' to the critique stage rather than a blanket ban.

findings.state: Briefing → saved monitoring rules → 'Review monitoring rule' when the request is vague, compound, low-confidence (<0.70) or unparseable
findings.current: Rendering is gated on `parse && parse.parse_succeeded && dispCopy`. For these inputs the Edge Function returns ok:true with parse_succeeded=false (parser.ts parseTriggerResponse demotes any success claim without a typed query; the prompt rule 6 tells the model not to commit a parsed_query below 0.70; rule 8 sets parse_succeeded=false for compound requests). parseDisposition returns "clarify_only" for every unsuccessful parse (parser.ts:549-551; triggers/_shared.ts:658-659).
findings.problem: When the parse does not succeed nothing renders: no error (r.ok is true), no ambiguities, no suggested_split, no parse_failure_reason, and the clarify_only copy 'This rule needs clarification before it can be enabled. Use the questions below to revise it.' never appears, because it sits inside the parse_succeeded block. The user clicks 'Review monitoring rule', the button returns to its idle label, and the screen is unchanged — exactly the cases the prompt deliberately routes to clarification (vague asks, 'X AND Y' compounds, 'soon/recently' without numbers). The user is blocked with no explanation.
findings.governing: AUDIT_BRIEF §5 (validation/error/partial-result states must not be swallowed); CLAUDE.md Part II §6 (loading/error never blank, never swallowed); comprehension principle
findings.proposed: Render the clarification state when the parse did not succeed: change the condition to `parse && dispCopy` and, inside, show the rephrase/meta lines only when parse.parse_succeeded; always show the ambiguities list; when parse.suggested_split is non-null show "This asks for more than one thing. Create a separate rule for each:" followed by the suggested_split items; when there are no ambiguities and no split, show parse.parse_failure_reason only if it is not one of the internal parser messages ('no JSON object found in response', 'JSON parse failed…', 'response root is not a JSON object', 'parser returned no usable query', 'parse did not succeed'), otherwise show "Antaeus could not turn that request into a monitoring rule. Name the company or category, the event, and a time window — for example: 'Tell me when two or more EOR competitors launch a product within 30 days.'" Add a component test for parse_succeeded=false with ambiguities and with suggested_split.

findings.state: Briefing → Review monitoring rule when the model call fails (Edge returns HTTP 502 {ok:false,error:'parser call failed: …'}) or the server throws (500)
findings.current: `if (error) { return { ok: false, …, error: error.message }; }` → AddTriggerFlow shows `r.error` verbatim (AddTriggerFlow.tsx:67). For a non-2xx response supabase-js sets error.message to its generic transport text ("Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code"); the server's own text, when it reaches the client, is technical ("parser call failed: …", "parse_trigger requires workspaceId + natural_language", raw exception messages).

findings.governing: CLAUDE.md Part II §6 / Part III §10 (error language: honest, calm, specific, recoverable); AUDIT_BRIEF §5 (fallbacks when AI/network is unavailable)
findings.proposed: In parseTriggerNL keep the technical message for reportError, and return a user message: on `error` or ok!==true → error: "Antaeus could not interpret that request right now because the language service did not respond.
